reason: Moll 2006 (BMJ): the source prints 64% vs 72% ovulation and arms of 111 and 114. The served counts 71/111 and 82/114 are the UNIQUE integers that round to those percentages (70/111 = 63.1%, 72/111 = 64.9%; 81/114 = 71.1%, 83/114 = 72.8%). The printed risk difference -8% (-20% to 4%) agrees with them (71/111 - 82/114 = -7.9 points). Recorded as a derivation, not a located count. The extractor's record fails verification only because it typed '- 8%' as a number; this ruling does not rely on that record.

derivation.rule: the unique integer k with round(100k/n) = printed %

population.span: To compare the effectiveness of clomifene citrate plus metformin and clomifene citrate plus placebo in women with newly diagnosed polycystic ovary syndrome.

endpoint.span: The primary outcome measure was ovulation.

estimate_ci.span: The ovulation rate in the metformin group was 64% compared with 72% in the placebo group, a non-significant difference (risk difference - 8%, 95% confidence interval - 20% to 4%).

arms.span: 111 women were allocated to clomifene citrate plus metformin (metformin group) and 114 women were allocated to clomifene citrate plus placebo (placebo group).

gap_follow_up.span: Patients continued to take the study medication until they had a positive pregnancy test or six ovulatory cycles or developed clomifene citrate resistance, whichever came first.

gap_entry_age.span: We excluded women with other causes of anovulation, age > 40 years,

entry_population.why: women with newly diagnosed PCOS (the ISRCTN55906981 parent is held)

typed_estimand.analysis_set: NOT STATED (denominators equal the allocated arms)
